bullets.title: NVDA crushes Q2 with blowout FY28 guide; stock +6-7% pre-market
bullets.body: NVDA reported $96.2B revenue (+106% YoY, beat by ~$4B), Data Center $89B (+117% YoY), and EPS $2.22 vs. $2.09 consensus. More importantly, management guided FY28 revenue to +70% YoY (~$695-710B) — well above the ~45% Street consensus — characterized as supply-constrained, with unconstrained demand tracking closer to +100%. Gross margins reset to 72-73% in FY28 (troughing at 71-72% in Jan-Q) due to HBM cost inflation, partially offset by price hikes; 96% of analysts rate Buy with average PT raised to ~$325. NVDA also agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9B and launched a $500B+ financing platform with capital providers.

bullets.title: NVDA supply chain read-through: memory tight through CY28, substrates fully booked, AI infra bottlenecks broadening
bullets.body: NVDA's guide implies 19-20GW of shipments in CY27 vs. ~13GW this year, with revenue/GW rising from $25B (Blackwell) to $40B (Vera Rubin). Supply commitments surged to $279B from $119B QoQ, primarily memory procurement locked through 2027. ABF substrates and PCB/CCL cited as the binding 2027 constraint — HBM reduction cannot circumvent it. DRAM seen under-supplied until Q2'28; NAND until Q4'27. Memory bull thesis (MU, Samsung, SK Hynix) reinforced; Samsung and SK Hynix expanding HBM4 8-stack share.

bullets.title: Broad software earnings wave: CRWD, CRM, OKTA all beat with AI monetization inflecting
bullets.body: CrowdStrike NNARR +51% YoY to $333M (biggest beat ever); FY27 ARR guide raised to $6.61B. Salesforce cRPO +14% CC, Agentforce ARR at $1.5B (+240% YoY), announced ClaudeForce with Anthropic; FY27 revenue raised $300M. Okta cRPO +14% YoY (3pts ahead), large enterprise wins +22% YoY, new products 30% of bookings; FY27 FCF guide 28-29%. SaaS sentiment shifting sharply positive as 'SaaSpocalypse' fears fade and AI monetization becomes measurable.

bullets.title: Fed: Core PCE at 3.3% in July, above 2% target for 65th straight month; Warsh Jackson Hole speech Friday is key macro catalyst
bullets.body: Core PCE advanced 3.3% YoY in July — still well above the Fed's 2% target — though 3- and 6-month annualized rates and the Dallas Fed trimmed mean point toward disinflation. Morgan Stanley raised 4Q/4Q core PCE forecast to 3.2%, near the 3.3% threshold where half the FOMC saw rate hikes as warranted in June, and flagged the no-hike call is 'closer than before.' Markets await Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech Friday for signals on the easing-to-neutral pivot; a supportive tone would be risk-positive and gold/bitcoin-favorable at the dollar's expense.

bullets.title: S&P 500 futures +0.4-0.5%, NDX +0.9% pre-market on tech earnings wave; 2Q earnings season nearly complete at 78% beat rate
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures +33bps (7723 handle) and NDX +0.9% Thursday morning on NVDA, CRM, CRWD, and OKTA earnings beats. 95.4% of S&P 500 market cap has reported 2Q26 results; 78% of companies topped estimates with aggregate EPS growth of 34.6% YoY (TECH+ segment +53.4% YoY). The Russell 2000 is up 21.1% YTD, outperforming the S&P 500 by 9.0%; 84% of Russell 2000 market cap has reported, tracking 0.1% above expectations with revenues +3.5%.

bullets.title: Trump weighing sweeping semiconductor tariffs; relief possible for US-investing companies
bullets.body: The Trump administration is considering a new round of sweeping tariffs on semiconductors, laptops, and servers per Politico, with a potential phase-in period. Companies investing in US chip manufacturing may receive relief. This is an overhang for the sector but also cited as a near-term positive catalyst for domestic-focused names. Senator Moreno separately proposed tariffs on South Korea over Coupang treatment.

bullets.title: META $18B teen social media settlement removes major regulatory overhang
bullets.body: Meta agreed to pay up to $18B over 10 years to settle multi-state teen safety lawsuits, with $10B accrued as a Q3 charge. Approximately $5.3B of the obligation is contingent on YouTube, TikTok, and Snap also settling. Teens account for less than 1% of Meta's revenue and spend ~1 hour/day on Meta apps, so operational impact is modest. META is planning its Watermelon AI agent platform launch for October 2026 with claimed GPT-5.5 parity. Stock up ~1.7% on the news.

bullets.title: BOJ signals rate hike readiness; Deputy Governor Himino warns against waiting too long
bullets.body: BOJ Deputy Governor Himino delivered hawkish commentary: could speed up rate hikes if financial conditions remain too accommodative, warns against waiting too long as delayed tightening risks a sharp inflation surge. Japan's 10-year JGB yield rose to 2.90%. Real borrowing costs remain negative in Japan. Key factors in BOJ's calculus include global AI demand (seen as boosting Japan's economy), FX movements (yen weakness driving inflation), and geopolitical risk.

bullets.title: Bank of Korea raises rates 25bps to 3.00%; signals gradual hike path amid elevated inflation
bullets.body: The Bank of Korea raised its policy rate to 3.00% from 2.75%, with one dissenting vote characterized as 'tactical' by Governor Shin. BOK forecasts 2026 GDP at 3.3% and inflation at 2.7%, expects inflation to stay above target for a prolonged period. The Korean won strengthened to 1,377/USD, its strongest since mid-September 2025. Governor Shin noted pre-emptive FX intervention is less costly than reactive measures.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure capex concerns: $12T financing need and AI datacenter policy headwinds create 2028+ earnings uncertainty
bullets.body: One macro note flags that the total AI infrastructure buildout requires ~$12T in financing and $7T in AI-related debt — additive to inflation and potentially forcing a slower buildout pace if financing constraints bind. Separately, Piper Sandler flagged SEI (power/energy infrastructure) is down 21% since Aug 17 due to AI datacenter moratoriums in TX, PA, MI ahead of midterms. Morgan Stanley's AI power basket forward PE has compressed to the 75th percentile despite strong EPS growth, as investors question whether the pace of investment is sustainable.

bullets.title: NVDA acquires Hugging Face for $12.9B; AWS deepens GPU partnership with 2M additional units
bullets.body: NVIDIA agreed to acquire the open-source AI model hub Hugging Face for $12.9B, ending Microsoft's prior talks. The deal secures NVDA's position in the open-source AI software ecosystem. Separately, AWS announced a major expansion of its NVIDIA partnership: 2M additional GPUs to be deployed across AWS global infrastructure through Q2 FY29, plus AI factories with 100K GPUs for the US government. OpenAI has committed ~12GW of NVDA compute through 2030.

bullets.title: Oil prices softening on Strait of Hormuz reopening hopes; WTI down ~6% on the week
bullets.body: WTI crude settled at ~$82.23/bbl, down roughly 6% on the week as Iran-Oman talks and recovering Hormuz shipping flows ease supply concerns. However, US allies privately warn the strait may still be mined, and UKMTO reported a tanker struck by a projectile during the window. Kuwait and Qatar increased crude shipments through the strait, helping stabilize prices. Russia-Ukraine escalation risk provides support.

bullets.title: Retailer earnings: DG beats/raises, DLTR and BURL disappoint on guidance despite tariff windfalls
bullets.body: Dollar General beat Q2 with +3.5% comps (90bps above buyside) and raised FY guidance ~5%. Dollar Tree beat on comps (+3.7%) with positive traffic for the first time since Q2'25, but Q3/Q4 EPS guidance underwhelmed as tariff benefits are reinvested without assumed sales lift. Burlington's +2% comp missed the +3% buyside expectation; 3Q guide +1-3% also soft. Best Buy delivered +4.1% comps vs +1.1% consensus, raising FY EPS to $6.70-6.90.

bullets.title: Gold +14% in August; dollar debasement and Jackson Hole uncertainty driving precious metals bid
bullets.body: Gold climbed to ~$4,635/oz (up ~14% in August) on ETF inflows and fiscal debasement concerns tied to 5-6% US deficits, $4T AI capex, and reshoring initiatives. Macro observers note gold/bitcoin are favored if Warsh signals easy financial conditions at Jackson Hole. The CBO also warned that US debt will reach 175% of GDP within 30 years.

bullets.title: Trump bans foreign energy equipment from US grid; Army awards $2.2B nuclear microreactor contract
bullets.body: Trump signed an executive order banning certain foreign-made (primarily Chinese) energy equipment from the US power grid on national security grounds, with DOE given 120 days to implement rules. Separately, the US Army awarded up to $2.2B over five years to five companies (Antares, BWXT, General Atomics, Radiant, Westinghouse) for nuclear microreactors at five military bases, potentially deploying 20+ reactors.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure supply chain: COHR sees 12-18 month optical shortage; substrates fully booked through 2026
bullets.body: At Jefferies' Global Semis Conference, Coherent described optical demand as 'extraordinary' with a supply shortage expected for 12-18+ months and potential capacity needs beyond 4x current plans. CPO adoption pushed to 2H CY28-CY30, creating near-term opening for NPO architectures. 1.6T transceiver shipments tracking toward 100M units in CY27. Semiconductor substrate capacity is fully booked through 2026 with 12-14 month lead times; 2027 bottleneck is ABF substrates and PCB/CCL.

bullets.title: INTC upbeat on 18A yields at DB conference; EMIB packaging emerges as TSMC rival
bullets.body: Intel presented upbeat commentary at Deutsche Bank's conference with 18A yields tracking ahead of targets and positive tone on process node development. Separately, Intel's EMIB advanced packaging has been confirmed as a rival to TSMC CoWoS with strong yields; Google and MediaTek are satisfied customers. Intel's 14A D0 performance curve tracking similar to Intel 22nm (described as its best node ever).

bullets.title: Chinese yuan at strongest since January 2023; China AI models gain ground on global leaderboards
bullets.body: The Chinese yuan reached its strongest level vs. the USD since January 2023. China's PBOC injected 503.5B yuan via overnight repos. On the AI competitive front, Zhipu's GLM-5.3-Flash achieved the top ranking on OpenRouter at $0.15/$0.50 per million tokens, and Alibaba released Qwen3.8-Flash claiming performance parity with Anthropic Opus 4.6 — Alibaba has committed $57B to AI over three years.

bullets.title: Atlanta Fed GDPNow raises 3Q26 real GDP estimate to +4.6%; Q2 GDP unrevised at +1.5%
bullets.body: The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model upgraded its 3Q26 real GDP estimate to +4.6% from +4.0%, supported by strong consumer spending and business investment data. Q2 GDP was confirmed at an unrevised +1.5% annualized pace with strength in consumer spending and business investment. The robust growth backdrop is seen supporting continued job creation but adding inflationary pressure that narrows the Fed's margin for error.

bullets.title: MRVL reports after the close Thursday; setup seen as positive on Google partnership and datacenter upside
bullets.body: Multiple buy-side and sell-side notes frame MRVL as positioned for a beat on AI/custom ASIC momentum. The Google partnership is seen worth $20B p.a. vs. prior buyside expectation of ~$12B in FY27 revenue; custom AI ASIC business modeled to double to $4B in FY28. MRVL has an 8.8% implied earnings-day move and is trading at 35x F28E EPS. JPM and Opco see Street estimates as a floor with potential for $11-12 EPS power by CY28.
